sets.relationshipLabel: a category of camp gear and one specific kind of it
sets.explanation: A tool and a vehicle are both broad categories, and a pickaxe and a sled are specific items that belong to each.

sets.relationshipLabel: a tool and the motion it exists to perform
sets.explanation: A pan exists to sift and a sluice exists to wash — each tool is defined by the single motion it was built to do.

sets.relationshipLabel: the start and end of one continuous span
sets.explanation: A freeze ends in a thaw just as a stampede of miners ends in a ghost town — each pair bookends the same rise-and-fall arc at a different scale.

sets.relationshipLabel: the small thing that necessarily enables the larger thing
sets.explanation: A match is what makes a campfire possible and a lantern is what makes visibility possible — each small object is the necessary cause of the larger condition.

glossary.definition: a long angled trough that uses flowing water to separate heavy material from loose dirt and gravel

definitions.definition: Any object made to help you do a job, like digging or building.
A heavy tool with a pointed head for breaking up rock and hard ground.
Anything used to carry people or goods from one place to another.
A flat frame on runners for hauling loads or people over snow and ice.
A shallow metal dish used to shake dirt and gravel while looking for gold.
To shake something through or around so the finer bits separate from the coarse.
A long trough that channels water to separate gold from gravel and sand.
To rinse or flush material with moving water, carrying away the lighter stuff.
A stretch of bitter cold weather that locks up ground and water.
The warming spell when ice and frozen ground soften and melt again.
A sudden rush of people all chasing the same opportunity at once.
A once-busy town left empty after everyone who came for it has gone.
A small stick that bursts into flame when struck against a rough surface.
A controlled fire built outdoors for warmth, cooking, or light.
A portable case holding a flame or bulb, carried to light your way.
How well you can see things around you in the dark or in bad weather.
